title: Edge & Private Deployments: Field Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose
- One-pager / mini-deck for field reps and SEs to surface Redwood Private and edge-hosted options during early discovery and technical scoping.
- Focus: when to recommend Private (VPC/on-prem) vs Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted API for edge/regulated scenarios.
- Status: working draft — sections marked [TODO] for tech verification.

Target audience
- SDR/BDR qualifying calls: short checklist + 2-3 lead questions.
- AE discovery + SE technical scoping: talking points, constraints matrix, demo checklist.
- Customer success: handoff notes for onboarding/sizing.

Quick TL;DR for opening lines (elevator)
- "If your app needs inference close to where data lives, or you must keep traffic inside a customer network (VPC or air-gapped), Redwood Private gives the same API and rollout controls as our hosted API while letting you put inference where the data is."
- Key differentiators to call out early: same developer API, configurable SLAs on Dedicated, KMS/HSM options, and an on-prem package for regulated environments.

Use-case framing (how to qualify)
- Ask these early:
  - "Does data need to remain in your VPC or on-prem?" (if yes -> Private)
  - "Do you have strict compliance policies requiring customer-controlled keys or air-gapped inference?" (if yes -> Private on-prem/HSM)
  - "Do you expect spiky but predictable throughput where dedicated GPUs are more cost-effective?" (if yes -> Dedicated)
  - "Is latency sensitivity sub-50ms end-to-end or local inference required?" (if yes -> edge or private colocation)

50s qualifying script for SDRs
- Intro: "We help teams run LLMs reliably at production scale — quick question: where does your inference need to run relative to your data and users?"
- If customer says "Inside our private network" -> "We offer Private deployments with VPC peering and on-prem options; can I connect you to an SE to scope network and key management needs?"
- If customer says "We need fast local inference (retail kiosk/warehouse)" -> "We have options for edge deployments and Dedicated pools — what's your throughput window?"

Objection handling (common friction points)
- "We already have GPUs/ops":
  - Response: "Great — Redwood Private is designed to integrate with customer infrastructure. We provide a control plane for model versioning/rollouts and runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache) so you don't rebuild tooling."
  - Ask: "Do you currently manage model rollouts and automatic fallbacks?"
- "We can't move data out of our network":
  - Response: "Our Private package supports VPC-only control planes and an on-prem runtime; keys can be managed via your KMS/HSM."
- "Costs seem high compared to self-hosting":
  - Response: "For edge/regulated workloads, the cost delta often reflects operational overhead you currently absorb; Redwood reduces engineering drift (rollouts, tracing, fallbacks) and gives predictable SLOs."

Competitive callouts (short)
- Incumbent cloud vendors: likely simpler for lift-and-shift hosted endpoints but weaker for air-gapped or private control plane requirements.
- Open-source stacks/self-host: full control but no unified developer API, rollouts, or support for automated fallback/cost optimizations.
- Other vendors offering private deployments: call out where Redwood stands out — consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in quality monitoring and rollback tooling, and focus on predictable inference economics.

Technical scoping matrix (cheat-sheet for SEs)
- Data residency: VPC-only / on-prem / hybrid
- Key management: customer KMS / Redwood-managed / HSM required
- Network constraints: outbound allowed? push/pull models?
- Latency SLO: <50ms / 50–200ms / >200ms
- Throughput pattern: steady / spiky / bursty (peak qps)
- Model catalog: open model allowed? licensed model required?
- Storage and artifacts: local checkpointing allowed?
- Compliance: SOC2/ISO/GDPR/PCI/PHI needs

Demo checklist (SE-ready)
- Pre-demo prep: confirm network access, example payloads, and size of sample inputs.
- Short local demo flow (15 min):
  1) Show API parity: same request/response between hosted and private.
  2) Show rollout UI: canary -> A/B -> full with rollback.
  3) Show observability: per-route latency/cost breakdown and token-level tracing.
  4) Show fallback policy in action: simulate capacity constraint and auto-fallback to cheaper variant.
  5) (If applicable) Walk through KMS integration and HSM note.

Pricing and procurement signals to watch for
- Customer mentions committed spend or preferring subscription contracts -> route to Dedicated pricing discussion.
- Procurement asks about seat-based licensing or enterprise support -> bring in Solutions/Contracts.
- Regulated industries asking for audit logs, retention policies -> mention compliance add-ons.

Hand-off template to Customer Success (mini SOP)
- Summary: short one-liner — "Private deployment scoped for [customer], requires VPC peering, KMS, X GPU nodes initial."
- Known constraints: egress blocked, approval for infra changes, procurement timeline.
- Starter artifacts: network diagram, sample payloads, compliance checklist.
- Next steps: schedule technical kickoff (SE + infra + customer infra lead), assign CSM.

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- [TODO] Confirm on-prem installation checklist for air-gapped customers (storage footprint, base OS, supported GPUs). Owner: Diego Morales.
- [TODO] Finalize pricing language for mixed Dedicated + Private deals (billing model when using both). Owner: Sofia Ramirez.
- [TODO] Add short script and screenshots for KMS/HSM integration. Owner: Liam Chen.

Appendix A — Short battlecard snippets (one-liners to keep in your head)
- "Same API. Different placement. Keep your code — move where it runs."
- "Private deployment = VPC + control plane + audit logs + optional air-gapped runtime."
- "Dedicated is for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Private is for data residency and compliance."

Appendix B — Quick links and refs
- Confluence: EDGE-ops-playbooks-42 (detailed tech runbook)
- JIRA: GTM-8123 (pricing and packaging for private/dedicated combos)
- Slack: #edge-sales-thread (recent field notes)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc intentionally short — field folks want bullets, not full runbooks.
- After initial round of field feedback, convert to 6-slide deck + 1-page cheat sheet.
- Include 2 short customer stories (anonymized) showing cost and compliance wins.

End of draft.
